trust_decision.summary: Whether a URL that arrived in the create-session response may become the executor's HTTP client target. After the fix the decision is made in AppiumCommandExecutor.overrideServerUrl through DirectConnectUrlSafety.requireSafeOverrideTarget (all resolved addresses must be non-loopback, non-link-local, non-unspecified, non-multicast); at the pinned commit the override is performed with no address decision at all, only the https-only protocol rule in setDirectConnect.

landing_point.why: The advisory names directConnect inside AppiumCommandExecutor; setDirectConnect is the place where create-session response fields become a URL and get handed to overrideServerUrl, which swaps the HttpClient.

fix_sites.entry_point: AppiumDriver/AndroidDriver/IOSDriver/Mac2Driver/WindowsDriver/GeckoDriver/ChromiumDriver/SafariDriver/Flutter*Driver (AppiumClientConfig, Capabilities) constructors with AppiumClientConfig.directConnect(true) -> new session -> createSession -> setDirectConnect -> overrideServerUrl
new internal helper DirectConnectUrlSafety.requireSafeOverrideTarget, reached only from overrideServerUrl

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The BiDi endpoint is an opt-in capability the caller explicitly requests (webSocketUrl), it is a WebSocket client rather than the HTTP command client the advisory names, and the advisory/fix are written purely about the directConnect redirect - so a solver can argue BiDi was never covered by this protection.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: directConnect exists to repoint the client at another Appium host - typically a private/on-prem grid host (10.x/192.168.x) and 127.0.0.1 in dev - and DirectConnect.isValid only requires the four fields to be non-null; a fix that rejects all private/RFC1918/CGNAT/ULA addresses (or every unresolvable hostname) breaks that feature, which is why the published javadoc explicitly keeps those accepted.

O6_input_shapes: empty or missing host in the URL

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The webSocketUrl capability returned in the create-session response is turned into a URI and used as the base URI of a newly created HttpClient for BiDi, with no loopback/link-local/unspecified/multicast check - only a non-null scheme check.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: BiDi is an opt-in capability feature (caller must ask for webSocketUrl), the endpoint is a WebSocket connection rather than the HTTP command client, and the advisory only describes the directConnect redirect, so it can be argued to be out of the advisory's scope.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: one file and one package away: io.appium.java_client.AppiumDriver vs io.appium.java_client.remote.AppiumCommandExecutor; reached from the same startSession flow that produces the directConnect fields, but the published fix never touches this file

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Apply the same address-class check to the BiDi webSocketUrl before the ws HttpClient is created (both the AppiumCommandExecutor branch and the default-factory branch).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Both values come from the very same new-session response, so a maintainer hardening 'server-supplied URL' would plausibly guard this path too - and it is exactly what the uncovered-route case needs.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Validate inside DirectConnect.getUrl() so any consumer of the parsed directConnect fields is covered, not only the override call site.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: getUrl() is the single place where the four untrusted response fields become a URL; a maintainer could reasonably put the guard there as defence in depth, which would leave the overrideServerUrl sink open for any other caller.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A guard in baseUrl(URL)/baseUri(URI) that every client construction inherits.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: baseUrl/baseUri is the funnel used by the command executor, the BiDi client and StorageClient, so a maintainer bolting the check there gets broad coverage - at the cost of also applying it to caller-supplied URLs, which is the over-broad trap.

O9_family: SSRF / confused deputy (CWE-918, CWE-441): unvalidated URL supplied by the remote server is followed by the client

O10_build.toolchain: Gradle 9.4.1 wrapper (gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties:3), source/target Java 11 (build.gradle:47-52), Selenium 4.42.0 (gradle.properties:3), JUnit Jupiter 5.14.3 via JvmTestSuite (build.gradle:213-231); dependencies resolve from Maven Central at build time
O10_build.project_tests: JUnit 5 unit tests under src/test run by the default 'test' suite. The directConnect area is covered by src/test/java/io/appium/java_client/internal/DirectConnectTest.java:17-38 (response map -> URL assembly) and src/test/java/io/appium/java_client/remote/AppiumCommandExecutorTest.java:37-40, which calls the protected overrideServerUrl from the same package; that pinned test uses the DNS name direct.example.com, and the published fix had to change it to the IP literal 203.0.113.1 because the new check resolves the host. The 'test' suite additionally depends on selenium-chrome-driver and webdrivermanager (build.gradle:233-239); the src/e2e*Test source sets need real devices and are separate.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Validate only the directConnect response fields in setDirectConnect or DirectConnect.getUrl (or hard-reject every non-public address), which leaves the protected overrideServerUrl sink open to other callers and breaks legitimate directConnect to private grid hosts.

out_of_scope_notes: The debugging constructor AppiumDriver(URL remoteSessionAddress, String platformName, String automationName) (src/main/java/io/appium/java_client/AppiumDriver.java:159-179) builds an executor around a caller-supplied URL with no address check, but that URL is user intent, not a server-supplied redirect, so it is outside this advisory.
